subject: Discovery recap: Observability + Evals (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, regression alerts)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Lowe <jenna@healthcareinc.com>, Marcus Reed <m.reed@healthcareinc.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability + Evals (dashboards, tracing, golden prompts, regression alerts)

Hi Jenna / Marcus

Thanks again for your time today. Wanted to recap the key takeaways from our discovery so we have a shared plan and next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong or that you'd like expanded.

Summary of pain points
- Limited visibility into model behavior in prod: token-level latency/cost breakdowns are hard to attribute to routes and prompt variants.
- No consistent evals/regression pipeline: QA relies on ad-hoc prompts and spreadsheet tracking, making it slow to detect performance regressions after model rollouts.
- Rollouts feel risky: no automatic guardrails for canarying or rollback based on quality regressions.

Current stack / integration points you mentioned
- Inference: in-house serving on AWS EKS with SageMaker endpoints for heavy jobs.
- Logging/metrics: partial integration with Datadog for infra metrics; application-level traces are limited.
- CI/evals: manual golden prompt sets maintained in internal Google Sheets; no automated regression alerts.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for HealthCare Inc)
1) Observability: per-route dashboards showing latency, token breakdown, and cost; trace links that map requests back to prompts and model version.
2) Evals: ability to run daily/weekly golden prompt suites, score pass/fail thresholds, and receive regression alerts that can trigger an automatic rollback or pause of a rollout.
3) Rollouts: canary/A-B capability with automatic quality gates and easy fallback to a stable variant.
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and VPC/private deployment options for PHI-sensitive workloads.

Specific deliverables I will share
- Redwood Console mock dashboard focused on token-level cost and latency per route (attached).
- Starter golden prompt set template (hc-eval-golden-prompts.xlsx attached) and suggested eval metrics.
- Short technical plan for tracing hooks and how they map to your Datadog traces.

Proposed next steps
1) I'll send the dashboard mock and golden prompt template (attached) action: Marissa (today).
2) Schedule a 45-min technical session with Monica (SE) to walk through tracing hooks and integration points with your EKS/SageMaker setup action: Jenna to propose availability this week.
3) Security packet & SOC2 artifacts: loop in Rachel (security) and send itemized evidence required action: Rachel to follow up within 48 hours after we confirm scope.
4) Pilot plan: 2-week eval on a subset of routes (50k tokens/day) with regression alerts enabled agree on KPIs and rollback thresholds.

Attaching the dashboard PDF and prompt template. We can tighten the pilot scope after the tech session.

Thanks  talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. This captures the call well. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Pilot scope  the routes we care most about initially are: insurance-eligibility-check, prior-auth-assist, and patient-summary-generation. We think a 2-week pilot that includes those three will show value.
2) Metrics  for our security/compliance team we'd need to show how traces are stored and access-controlled. SOC2 artifacts are a must before we move beyond a pilot.
3) Pricing  can you send a rough pilot pricing estimate (ballpark for 50k tokens/day for two weeks and a short-run dedicated instance if needed)? We need this to get internal approval.
4) Scheduling  Marcus and I are available Wed/Thu mornings PST for the SE deep-dive.

Next steps for us: I'll confirm availability Wed morning and share a short list of regulatory questions for Rachel.

Thanks, looking forward to the demo.
— Jenna Lowe
